description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of mathematical problems across different educational levels and subject areas within the MathOdyssey benchmark, totaling 387 problems as indicated by the sum of the numerical values in parentheses. The largest segment corresponds to “Algebra – Olympiad-level” at 21.19% (82 problems), followed by “Pre-Calculus – High School” at 14.21% (55 problems), and “Algebra – High School” at 17.83% (69 problems). Other notable segments include “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level” (9.56%, 37 problems), “Geometry – Olympiad-level” (6.46%, 25 problems), and “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level” (6.46%, 25 problems). Smaller segments represent “Calculus and Analysis – University-level” (6.20%, 24 problems), “Probability – University-level” (5.43%, 21 problems), “Statistics – University-level” (4.39%, 17 problems), “Differential Equations – University-level” (3.62%, 14 problems), “Geometry – High School” (3.62%, 14 problems), and “Number Theory – Olympiad-level” (1.03%, 4 problems). Each slice is labeled with its category, percentage, and problem count, and the chart uses distinct colors for visual differentiation, with no slices exploded or emphasized. The segments are arranged clockwise in descending order of size, providing a clear visual hierarchy of problem distribution by topic and educational level.
